issue.title: gateway: /v1/systemone sends its body upstream without redaction
issue.body:
## Problem

With `redact: true`, a body sent to `POST /v1/systemone` goes to the decision provider unmasked. A secret in `state` reaches api.typesafe.ai as the client wrote it.

## Cause

Masking runs only where a handler calls `redacted()` (`internal/gateway/redact.go`). `serve()` does it at `gateway.go:1481`, so `/v1/messages`, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` are masked, and so is the routing classifier, which runs inside `serve()` after that call. `serveSystemOne` (`decide.go:441`) never calls it: it reads the body and hands it to `postDecide` (`decide.go:531`) as is. A decision group takes the same unmasked body, since `serveSystemOne` passes it to `serveDecisionGroup` (`decide.go:464`), which posts it to each member (`decide_group.go:155`). `MaskJSON` would catch `state` fine; the body just never gets there.

## Repro

On v0.1.1254, redact on, typesafe provider:
- `/v1/messages` to a Claude model with a fake `ghp_…` token: the model sees a `{{…}}` placeholder.
- `/v1/systemone` to `typesafe/jev-latest` with fake `sk-…`, `ghp_…` and `AKIA…` tokens in `state`, asking Jev whether it sees the raw value or a placeholder: raw, confidence 0.98–1.0, for all three.

## Fix

Follow what `serve()` does (`gateway.go:1476-1481`, `1688`):
- In `serveSystemOne`, call `redacted(w, body)` once, after `refuseOff` and before `decisionGroupOf`, so both the single-model and the group branch get the masked body. Keep the original as `plain`, and fail closed on error.
- After the route is known, send `plain` where `unredactedRoute` allows it: `unredactedRoute(p, false, nil)` after `RouteDecider`, and `unredactedRoute(provider.Provider{}, true, ms)` in the group branch.
- If the handler writes through the returned writer, `defer` its `done`. The answer carries no request text, so restoring is not needed, but `done` writes what the wrapper still holds (`redact.go:12-16`).

comments.body:
**Root cause:** `serve()` calls `redacted()` before routing (`gateway.go`), but `serveSystemOne` never did — it passed the raw body into `postDecide` / `serveDecisionGroup`, so with `redact: true` a secret in `state` reached the decision provider unmasked.

**Change:** After `refuseOff`, call `redacted` once (fail closed), keep `plain`, and send `plain` only when `unredactedRoute` allows it (single model and decision group). Same pattern as `serve()`.

**Test red without the fix** (`HOME=$(mktemp -d) go test -tags nogui -count=1 -run TestSystemOneRedactsStateBeforeUpstream ./internal/gateway/`):
```
--- FAIL: TestSystemOneRedactsStateBeforeUpstream (0.03s)
    systemone_redact_test.go:62: upstream saw the raw secret: {"model":"jev-latest",...,"state":{"message":"token sk-proj-abcdEFGH1234ijklMNOP5678qrst"}}
FAIL
```

**Checks run** (temporary `HOME`):
- `gofmt -l` — clean
- `go vet -tags nogui` + `go build -tags nogui` on linux, darwin/amd64, windows/amd64 — ok
- `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -run TestSystemOneRedactsStateBeforeUpstream ./internal/gateway/` — pass
- Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` — not run this round (known unrelated failures on clean main around bun/proxy)

**Compare / patch:**
- https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...ump45nose:magpie:fix/2389-systemone-redact
- https://github.com/ump45nose/magpie/commit/c3154fc19665975837bb9b90f396539883ed746d.patch
- Branch: `fix/2389-systemone-redact` @ `c3154fc1`

### AI assistance disclosure
An AI coding agent drafted the change and the regression test; I checked it against the issue’s serve()/redacted guidance, confirmed the test fails on current main without the fix and passes with it, and ran the gofmt/vet/build checks above.

Published a fix in my fork: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/ee1b018bdb21f67185fee59cc8d1b2c69aa21c4b

Thanks to @ump45nose for the diagnosis and original c3154fc1 patch, credited as co-author. I adapted it to the current routing and masking helpers. POST /v1/systemone now masks request bodies before either direct-provider dispatch or decision-group dispatch, restores masked values in responses, and preserves the existing explicit unredacted-provider exemption (a mixed group remains masked). Privacy-off behavior is unchanged. Blocking rules return 400; an unavailable required masker returns 503 without contacting an upstream. The routing reference documents the contract.

Ten handler-level regression scenarios cover direct and group requests, group failover, single/all/mixed provider exemptions, privacy off, and blocked/unavailable-masker behavior on both paths. Seven scenarios fail against the old product code, including raw-secret leakage and requests reaching upstream when they should be rejected. With the fix all ten pass, as do related masking and decision tests under -race -count=5.

At this exact head, all seven acceptance commands passed with Go1.26.8, isolated HOME and pinned caches: native Linux vet/build, Linux nogui vet/build, Windows vet/build, and go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m (69 packages). Gofmt and whitespace checks are clean.

Combined branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/issue-batch-20261023-v

Not checked: a live provider, GUI interaction, or macOS/Windows runtime. The regression uses local mock upstreams and an isolated masking fixture. No live gateway/config changed and no upstream PR opened. Leaving confirmation of the reporter's real provider to the reporter.

Still live on a build I pulled today, verified end to end from a real client rather than by asking Jev what it saw.

The caller in my case is Hindsight's TypeSafe reranker, which posts to `{base}/v1/systemone` with `model: "jev-latest"` and the candidate documents in `state`. Chain: client → gateway A → this gateway → decision provider. With `redact: true` and `redactPersonal: true`:

- `state.message` carrying an email, a phone number and a public IPv4 → **200**, answer came back normally.
- Masking record count before and after: **168 → 168**. Nothing added.
- Records with `what: "decide"` on that gateway: **0**, ever.

The second point is what makes it conclusive rather than just "no record appeared": the classifier path on the same gateway *does* write `what: "decide"` records, so masking runs there and only the public endpoint is the gap. `noteMaskedUntil` returns early when nothing was swapped, so a silent log alone proves little — the absence of any `decide` record from a payload that certainly had PII does.

One note on the fix, since `decide.go` has grown since this was filed: `maskedState` (added 2026-10-17, "what Jev is told of a turn is masked unless Jev itself may have it unmasked") already does the masking this endpoint needs — it masks `state` text, the user's message and the previous reply, fails closed, and records under `decide`. `serveSystemOne` just doesn't call it. Reusing it there would be a much smaller change than threading `redacted()` through the single-model and group branches separately, and would leave both paths recording under one name.

`/v1/rerank` and `/v1/embeddings` do mask, for what it's worth — I checked those on the same gateway and both write records. This endpoint is the only retrieval-ish surface left unmasked.

The endpoint never reached the masker, and it wrote no masking record: `serve()` masks a conversation at the one place every request passes (`gateway.go:1690`) and records it (`gateway.go:2402`), while `serveSystemOne` (`internal/gateway/decide.go:510`) handed the body straight to `postDecide`/`serveDecisionGroup`. So with `redact: true` a document under `state` went to the decision provider as written, and no `what: "decide"` record could exist for it. The records on the classifier come from `askJev` -> `maskedState` -> `noteMasked(nil, "decide", ...)`, a different call. One addition to your count: `redactedHits` records nothing by itself (it only marks the redaction phase), so even a masked body on this route would have left 168 -> 168; what your check establishes is the missing record.

The branch masks the body once in `serveSystemOne`, after `refuseOff` and before either branch, so a single model and every member a decision group tries get the masked body, and records what it swapped with `noteMasked(..., "decide", ...)` - the same `what` the classifier's requests use. Placeholders in the answer are restored through the same writer. `unredactedRoute` still sends the original body only where the user set requests to go unmasked, and masking off is unchanged.

`maskedState` is not reused here on purpose: it masks the classifier's three texts in its own `jevBody`, not a client's arbitrary JSON, so a document under `state` is invisible to it. The whole-body JSON masker `serve()` uses (`redactedHits`, `MaskJSON`) is what this route needs.

[fix/2389-systemone-state-redaction](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2389-systemone-state-redaction), commit 05f768ef9bdb505b4eb02282ebae4a9d9de67cb7.

Run at that head, temporary HOME with pinned Go caches: `TestSystemOneMasksStateBeforeUpstream` fails on unmodified `decide.go` - the fake decision provider receives `"contact dana.reyes@northwind-logistics.com, call +14158675309, host 52.95.110.7"` - on both the single-model and the group-failover cases, and passes with the change, asserting no secret upstream and one `what: "decide"` record with three values; also green under `-race`. `gofmt` clean, `go build ./...` ok, `go vet` ok on `internal/gateway`. `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway -count=1` passes except five tests that fail the same on clean upstream/main with the change removed (fastjson U+2028/U+2029, a WSL host check, a Claude Code prompt check, the Codex image fit).

Fork branch, ready to review; it does not claim the issue.
